About Us

Building a Better Tomorrow, Together

Who We Are

SOS Foundation is the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) arm of SOS Group of Companies. It was established in 2017 under SOS Pakistan (Pvt.) Ltd. as a not-for-profit organisation. We work to improve the lives of underserved and marginalised communities across Pakistan through sustainable, community-driven development.

We are backed by the long-term commitment of SOS Group and our Board of Trustees. This brings corporate discipline, accountability and continuity to our social development work. We work alongside communities, government departments, civil society organisations and international development partners, so that our efforts complement national and provincial priorities.

Our Journey

Education and workforce development have been at the heart of our work since 2017. Through scholarships, teacher training and support for higher education, we have helped young people from low-income households continue their studies and build pathways to dignified employment. Our flagship initiative, the National University for Security Sciences (NUSS), Islamabad, has had its charter approved by both the National Assembly and the Senate of Pakistan.

Alongside education, we have responded to urgent basic needs. We have installed reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration plants and hand pumps that bring safe drinking water to underserved communities, and we run hunger-relief initiatives that provide meals and rations to vulnerable families. Today our work spans nine thematic programmes, from health and climate action to women's empowerment and human rights.

Our Vision

A world where every person can live with dignity, opportunity and hope, free from poverty and hardship.

Our Mission

To empower underserved communities through sustainable, partnership-driven initiatives in education, healthcare, clean water and livelihoods, so that they can move from hardship to self-reliance.

Our Core Values

Compassion

We put people first, serving every community with empathy, respect and care for human dignity.

Integrity

We act with honesty, transparency and fairness, and we honour the trust our partners and communities place in us.

Accountability

We take responsibility for our decisions, our use of resources and our results, and we report openly to communities, donors and partners.

Inclusion

We reach those most often left behind, including women, children, persons with disabilities and remote communities, without discrimination of any kind.

Collaboration

We believe lasting change comes from working together with communities, government, the private sector and development partners.

Innovation

We seek creative, evidence-based solutions that deliver lasting impact and can grow to reach more people.

Sustainability

We design programmes that communities can own and carry forward, so that impact lasts beyond our direct involvement.

RWU, SOS Foundation and NCHD Sign MoU to Promote Literacy

Rawalpindi Women University (RWU), SOS Foundation and the National Commission for Human Development (NCHD) have signed a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote literacy and increase access to education.

Representatives of all three organisations signed the agreement and exchanged the signed documents. Under the MoU, the partners will join hands on literacy programmes, awareness activities, and joint initiatives aimed at reducing illiteracy and supporting learners across the community.

The participants said that collaboration between academia, civil society, and government institutions is essential for achieving meaningful progress in education. They expressed the hope that the partnership would bring positive and lasting results.

Islamabad, 8 September 2026: On International Literacy Day, SOS Foundation organised a Literacy Walk from Mr. Books, F-6 Markaz to the National Press Club, Islamabad, to highlight the urgent issue of 26 million out-of-school children in Pakistan.

Students, teachers, social workers, and citizens joined the walk to advocate for Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan and UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG-4): Quality Education for All.

The participants called for collective action to raise awareness, inspire concrete steps, and ensure that every child's right to education is upheld.

SOS Foundation, ICCI and EduTransform Organise Teachers' Training Workshop on 21st Century Teaching Skills

Workshops and Trainings · 24 June 2026 · Islamabad

Islamabad, 24 June 2026: SOS Foundation, in collaboration with the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry (ICCI) and EduTransform, organised a one-day teachers' training workshop on 21st Century Teaching Skills at ICCI, Islamabad.

Sardar Tahir Mehmood, President ICCI, was the Chief Guest at the event, while H.E. Naeem Khan, Pakistan's Ambassador to Rwanda, graced the occasion as Guest of Honor and interacted directly with the participants.

Dr. Abdus Salam, CEO SOS Foundation, welcomed the participants. Dr. Aneela Malik, CEO EduTransform, conducted an insightful and highly engaging training session.

Educators from across the twin cities attended the workshop in large numbers. The participants appreciated the initiative and described it as the need of the hour for Pakistan's education landscape.

President ICCI Sardar Tahir Mehmood acknowledged and appreciated the efforts of SOS Foundation in organizing this important initiative.

Leadership

SOS Foundation is guided by a committed Board of Trustees and led by a management team with experience in education, development and organisational management.

Message from the Chairman

Building a better tomorrow, together

We live in a time of profound global challenges. With 2030 fast approaching, the world remains off track on most of the Sustainable Development Goals. Climate change is intensifying floods, heatwaves and droughts across the globe. Inequality is widening, conflicts and economic shocks are pushing millions back into poverty, and the poorest communities have the fewest means to cope.

Pakistan stands at the centre of many of these challenges. We contribute little to global emissions, yet we are among the nations most exposed to climate disasters, as the devastating floods of 2022 made clear. Millions of our children remain out of school, too many families lack safe drinking water and basic healthcare, and many women and young people are still denied the skills and opportunities they need to reach their full potential. At the same time, our young population is our greatest strength. With the right investment, it can become the driving force of a more prosperous and resilient Pakistan.

SOS Group of Companies established SOS Foundation in 2017 on a clear conviction: business success carries a responsibility to the society that makes it possible. For us, corporate social responsibility is not charity alone. It is a long-term investment in people, so that they can live with dignity, opportunity and self-reliance. The Foundation brings the discipline, accountability and continuity of the corporate sector to social development, working with government, academia, civil society and the private sector, because no single organisation can meet these challenges alone.

On behalf of the Board of Trustees, I affirm that SOS Foundation will always place the most vulnerable people and communities at the centre of its work. We will uphold the highest standards of integrity, transparency and accountability in the use of every resource entrusted to us, and we will measure our success by the lasting change we help create, not by short-term relief alone. In everything we do, we will contribute to Pakistan's national development priorities and to the global 2030 Agenda, and we will build partnerships that turn shared responsibility into shared progress.

I thank our partners, donors, volunteers and dedicated team, and above all the communities who place their trust in us. I invite you to join us in building a more equitable, resilient and prosperous future for Pakistan and beyond.

[Signature]

Kanwar M. Tariq

Chairman, Board of Trustees, SOS Foundation

Message from the Chief Executive Officer

From commitment to measurable impact

Welcome to SOS Foundation.

Pakistan's development challenges are well documented, and they demand serious, sustained and collective action. More than 25 million children aged 5 to 16 are out of school, over one-third of that age group¹. Only around 45% of the population uses safely managed drinking water². Female labour force participation stands at just 24.4%³, and the 2022 floods affected 33 million people⁴, a stark reminder of how climate change compounds poverty. Yet with 64% of our population under the age of 30⁵, Pakistan also holds one of the greatest demographic opportunities in the world, if we invest in our people today.

SOS Foundation exists to help turn that opportunity into reality. Our work is guided by the Constitution of Pakistan, including every child's right to free and compulsory education under Article 25-A, and by the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Every programme we design is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and with national development priorities, so that our efforts complement those of government and the wider development sector.

We believe development works best when it is led by communities, not delivered to them. We listen first, design solutions together and build local ownership, so that change continues long after our direct involvement ends. Our approach combines grassroots engagement with evidence-based planning, systematic monitoring and transparent reporting, so that every resource entrusted to us delivers verifiable results. Our partnerships with government institutions, universities, civil society, the private sector and development partners allow us to reach further, learn faster and scale what works.

As Chief Executive Officer, I am committed to leading SOS Foundation with integrity, professionalism and accountability. We will continue to strengthen our programmes, governance and systems in line with recognised standards of good practice in the non-profit sector. We will measure our success not by the activities we carry out but by the lives we help transform, and we will remain open and answerable to the communities, partners and donors who place their trust in us.

I am grateful to our Chairman and Board of Trustees for their vision and guidance, to our dedicated team for their commitment, and to every partner, donor and volunteer who stands with us. I warmly invite you to join us in building a better tomorrow, together.

[Signature]

Our Approach

Our Strategic Goals

  1. 1Expand access to quality education, healthcare and safe drinking water for underserved communities, and reach more individuals and families directly across all programmes.
  2. 2Build self-reliance through skills development, livelihoods and economic empowerment, with a special focus on women and youth.
  3. 3Strengthen resilience of vulnerable communities against disasters, climate change and economic shocks.
  4. 4Deliver measurable impact through evidence-based programming, monitoring and transparent reporting.
  5. 5Grow partnerships with government, corporate, academic and international partners to diversify our funding base and scale proven solutions.
  6. 6Pilot innovation by testing new interventions that respond to emerging community needs.

How We Work

Community-led

We design interventions with communities, not just for them, to ensure local ownership and lasting impact.

Partnership-driven

We collaborate with federal and provincial government bodies, academia, the private sector and development agencies to scale what works.

Results-focused

We track outcomes, not just activities, and report transparently to our stakeholders.

Accountable

Our governance, financial management and reporting reflect the standards of a responsible corporate group.

Our Guiding Principles

Dignity first

Every individual we serve is treated as a partner, not a recipient of charity.

Do no harm

Our interventions are designed to protect communities and never create new risks.

Neutrality

We serve people solely on the basis of need, regardless of religion, ethnicity, gender or political affiliation.

Safeguarding

We are committed to protecting children, women and vulnerable adults in all our programmes.

Transparency

We use every rupee responsibly and are open about how resources are spent.

Our Commitment

We stand with communities in their journey from hardship to hope, working with compassion, acting with integrity, and building a more equitable, resilient and prosperous Pakistan, one community at a time.

Human Rights

Dignity, equality and respect for all.

The Challenge

Human rights are the foundation of a just, peaceful and inclusive society. Yet many people in Pakistan, particularly in marginalised communities, remain unaware of their fundamental rights and face barriers to equality and full participation. SOS Foundation promotes awareness of the rights guaranteed under the Constitution of Pakistan and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and fosters a culture of dignity, equality, tolerance and mutual respect.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions); also SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

SDG 16SDG 4SDG 5SDG 10

What We Do

Human Rights Awareness and Education

Through sessions and workshops in educational institutions and communities, we educate young people about their fundamental rights and encourage them to uphold the rights of others.

Peace, Tolerance and Interfaith Harmony

We promote human fraternity, interfaith harmony and peaceful coexistence, building respect for every individual regardless of faith, ethnicity or social status.

Freedom of Expression and Responsible Digital Citizenship

We promote freedom of expression, access to accurate information and the responsible use of social media and emerging technologies, and we raise awareness among youth about misinformation.

Public Advocacy and Awareness Walks

Through public awareness walks and campaigns, we bring citizens together to call for equality, justice and dignity for all.

Health and Nutrition

Healthier communities, from prevention to care.

The Challenge

Pakistan faces a heavy burden of preventable disease and malnutrition. Around 40% of children under five are stunted, and Pakistan has the highest number of hepatitis C infections in the world, an estimated 8.8 million. Limited access to healthcare and low health awareness hit vulnerable communities hardest. SOS Foundation works to improve community health through medical outreach, preventive care, nutrition and support for families in need.

Source: National Nutrition Survey 2018 (Government of Pakistan, Aga Khan University and UNICEF); World Health Organization, Global Hepatitis Report 2024.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger); also SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

SDG 3SDG 2SDG 6SDG 10

What We Do

Free Medical Camps

We organise free medical camps in underprivileged areas, offering general consultations, basic diagnostic screening, free medicines and health education, with referrals for further treatment where needed.

Preventive Healthcare and Disease Awareness

With medical universities, hospitals and academic institutions, we run awareness sessions on the prevention, early detection and treatment of communicable diseases such as hepatitis and tuberculosis, and we promote stigma-free support for patients.

Nutrition and Food Safety

We promote balanced nutrition and safe food practices, including hygiene, safe food preparation and handling, to prevent food- and water-borne diseases.

Food Security and Hunger Relief

Through our hunger-relief initiatives, we provide nutritious meals and food support to vulnerable families, helping them meet their basic needs with dignity.

Drug Abuse Prevention

We raise awareness among youth and communities about the harms of drug abuse and promote prevention, rehabilitation and recovery through community action.

Livelihoods

From skills to sustainable income.

The Challenge

Pakistan is one of the youngest countries in the world: 64% of its population is under 30. Yet national unemployment has risen to 7.1%, its highest level in over two decades, and many young people, women and members of underserved communities lack market-relevant skills and decent work. SOS Foundation works to unlock this potential through skills development, employability and entrepreneurship, helping people move from dependence to dignity and self-reliance.

Source: UNDP, Pakistan National Human Development Report: Unleashing the Potential of a Young Pakistan; Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force Survey 2024-25.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth); also SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

SDG 8SDG 1SDG 5SDG 10

What We Do

Digital Skills and Online Earning

We promote digital and IT skills as pathways to employment, freelancing and online entrepreneurship, with a focus on youth and women.

Vocational and Technical Skills Training

We support training in market-relevant trades for youth outside formal education and for women from underserved communities, and encourage recognised skills certification.

Youth Employability and Soft Skills

Through seminars, career sessions and campus engagement, we help young people build soft skills, career readiness and confidence for the job market.

Entrepreneurship and Self-Employment

We encourage individuals and families to start small businesses and home-based enterprises, turning skills into sustainable household income.

Skills Partnerships and Policy Dialogue

We convene universities, skills institutions, government bodies and the private sector to strengthen collaboration on youth skills, adult literacy and pathways to employment.

Education for All

Every child in school. Every learner a future.

The Challenge

Education is a fundamental right and a cornerstone of social and economic development. Yet over 25 million children aged 5 to 16, about 35% of that age group, are out of school in Pakistan. National literacy stands at 60.7%, and only 52.8% for women, while 77% of ten-year-olds cannot read and understand a simple text. SOS Foundation works to close these gaps through inclusive, equitable and quality education and lifelong learning for children, youth and adults, upholding every child's constitutional right to education under Article 25-A.

Source: Pakistan Institute of Education, Pakistan Education Statistics 2023-24 and Public Financing in Education 2025-26; Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Census 2023.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 4 (Quality Education); also SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 5 (Gender Equality) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

SDG 4SDG 1SDG 5SDG 10

What We Do

Flagship Initiative: National University for Security Sciences (NUSS)

Our flagship higher education project is the National University for Security Sciences, Islamabad, whose charter has been approved by both the National Assembly and the Senate of Pakistan. NUSS is envisioned as a centre of excellence for higher education, research and professional development in security sciences and allied disciplines. It will soon begin operations and will develop skilled professionals and future leaders for Pakistan.

Scholarships and Higher Education Support

We provide scholarships and financial assistance to talented students facing financial hardship, helping them pursue education at school, college and university level.

Teacher Development

We build the capacity of educators through training workshops on modern pedagogy, 21st-century teaching skills and classroom management.

Out-of-School Children and Basic Education

We help out-of-school children return to learning through accelerated learning programmes, learning materials and partnerships with community-based schools.

Adult Literacy and Advocacy

Our adult literacy programme offers second-chance learning to adults with little or no formal education. Through public awareness walks, policy dialogues and national literacy campaigns, we also advocate for action on Pakistan's literacy and out-of-school challenges.

Girls' Education

We advocate for girls' right to education and work to remove the barriers that keep them out of school, including poverty, safety concerns, social norms and early dropout. Through campaigns, seminars and partnerships with academic institutions, we promote girls' education, leadership and careers in science and technology.

Educational Infrastructure

We support the establishment and renovation of schools and learning spaces in underserved areas, so that students can learn in safe and conducive environments.

Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)

Safe water, sanitation and hygiene for every home.

The Challenge

Safe water, proper sanitation and good hygiene are fundamental to health and dignity. Yet only around 45% of Pakistan's population uses safely managed drinking water, leaving millions exposed to preventable waterborne disease. Women and girls carry much of this burden, often spending long hours fetching water. SOS Foundation works to close these gaps through practical interventions, hygiene promotion and community participation.

Source: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, SDG indicator 6.1.1 (2024), via the UN-Water SDG 6 Data Portal.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation); also SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

SDG 6SDG 3SDG 11SDG 12

What We Do

Safe Drinking Water

We install reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration plants and water hand pumps in underserved communities, bringing safe drinking water closer to people's homes. Water quality is tested by recognised laboratories, including the National Institute of Health, to confirm it is fit for human consumption.

Sanitation and Drainage

We support small-scale sanitation and drainage improvements based on community needs, creating cleaner and safer living environments.

Hygiene Promotion Drive

Through our ongoing Hygiene Promotion Drive, we run interactive sessions in schools and communities on handwashing, personal and oral hygiene and household cleanliness, and provide hygiene supplies to help these habits stick.

Waste Management and Clean Surroundings

We promote waste segregation, recycling, composting of organic waste and avoiding waste burning, helping communities keep their surroundings clean and healthy.

Women Empowerment

Skilled, confident and economically independent women.

The Challenge

Women make up nearly half of Pakistan's population, yet remain among the most underrepresented groups in economic and public life. In the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Report 2026, Pakistan ranked 143rd of 145 economies and last in South Asia, with economic participation its weakest area at 144th. Female labour force participation stands at 24.4%, compared with 69.8% for men, and female unemployment at 10.5%, against 6.0% for men. SOS Foundation believes that empowering women is one of the most effective ways to lift families out of poverty.

Source: World Economic Forum, Global Gender Gap Report 2026; Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force Survey 2024-25.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 5 (Gender Equality); also SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

SDG 5SDG 4SDG 8SDG 10

What We Do

Vocational Skills Training

We run stitching, embroidery and other vocational classes for women and girls in underserved communities, providing sewing machines, materials and structured instruction.

Livelihood Support and Income Generation

We provide women with tools such as sewing machines and kitchen gardening kits to turn their skills into home-based income.

Rural Women Empowerment

We help women in rural and peri-urban communities explore practical livelihoods, including stitching, cooking, vegetable gardening and compost-making.

Education and Leadership Development

We promote women's access to education, higher learning and leadership, and encourage young women to pursue their academic and professional aspirations.

Women's Rights Awareness and Advocacy

Through seminars, conferences and awareness events with universities, government bodies and civil society, we advocate for women's rights, dignity and equal participation in decision-making.

Community Development

Communities that own their own development.

The Challenge

Strong, self-reliant communities are the foundation of inclusive development. Yet many underserved communities in Pakistan, rural and urban, still lack basic infrastructure, essential services, food security and livelihood opportunities. SOS Foundation works hand in hand with these communities, identifying needs together and delivering practical solutions that foster lasting community ownership.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities); also SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals).

SDG 11SDG 1SDG 2SDG 10SDG 17

What We Do

Community Infrastructure and Basic Services

We support small-scale infrastructure that responds directly to community needs, such as water hand pumps, drainage and improved access, reducing daily hardships, particularly for women and children.

Household Food Security and Kitchen Gardening

We encourage families to grow their own vegetables, providing plants and gardening tools to improve nutrition, reduce household expenses and earn small additional income from surplus produce.

Community Participation and Ownership

We involve residents in identifying priorities, planning interventions and maintaining shared resources, so every initiative is owned and sustained by the community itself.

Volunteerism and Community Giving

Through volunteer drives and giving campaigns, we mobilise students and citizens to share books, stationery and other essentials with children and families in need. We also encourage community members to turn small skills, such as tailoring, home-based food preparation and handicrafts, into small business opportunities, helping families earn a dignified livelihood rather than depend on aid.

Humanitarian Response

Standing with communities when crisis strikes.

The Challenge

Pakistan is highly exposed to floods, extreme weather and other climate-induced disasters. The 2022 floods alone affected 33 million people, claimed more than 1,730 lives and caused over USD 30 billion in damages and economic losses. SOS Foundation stands with affected communities in times of crisis, providing timely relief while building preparedness for long-term recovery.

Source: Government of Pakistan, World Bank, ADB, EU and UNDP, Post-Disaster Needs Assessment: Floods 2022.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and SDG 13 (Climate Action); also SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being).

SDG 1SDG 11SDG 13SDG 2SDG 3

What We Do

Emergency Relief

With universities and established welfare organisations, we mobilise and deliver food rations, clothing, bedding and other household essentials to disaster-affected families.

Seasonal and Winter Relief

We support displaced and flood-affected families with quilts, warm clothing and other essentials to help them through harsh winters.

Disaster Preparedness and Early Warning

We build awareness of disaster risk reduction, early warning systems and household preparedness, with a special focus on training young people.

Humanitarian Awareness and Youth Engagement

Through seminars and campus engagement, we promote humanitarian values and encourage young people to volunteer in support of vulnerable communities.

Climate Change and Community Engagement

Climate action that starts in our communities.

The Challenge

Pakistan contributes less than 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet Germanwatch's Climate Risk Index 2025 ranked it the country most affected by extreme weather in 2022. Melting glaciers, record heatwaves, drought, water scarcity, urban smog and deforestation increasingly threaten health, food security and livelihoods, with the poorest communities hit hardest. SOS Foundation believes climate action must begin at the community level, with youth, women and local communities as agents of change.

Source: Germanwatch, Climate Risk Index 2025.

SDG alignment: primarily SDG 13 (Climate Action); also SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

SDG 13SDG 11SDG 12SDG 15

What We Do

Green Pakistan Tree Plantation Drive

Every year, in collaboration with government departments, educational institutions, community organisations and corporate partners, we plant and distribute fruit-bearing and indigenous trees in homes, schools, universities, parks and public spaces. Families and volunteers take responsibility for caring for the plants, ensuring higher survival rates and lasting community ownership.

Green Spaces and Urban Greening

We develop and restore green spaces and support urban beautification to reduce urban heat and pollution and restore natural habitats.

Climate Awareness Seminars and Workshops

With universities, colleges and schools, we hold regular sessions on climate change, clean energy, smog, biodiversity, conservation, plastic pollution and desertification, turning awareness into practical action.

Awareness Walks and Public Campaigns

We mark international environmental days with awareness walks and public campaigns that carry the message of climate action into streets and neighbourhoods.

Youth and Volunteer Engagement

We mobilise students, interns and community volunteers through plantation drives, clean-ups, environmental competitions and campus green clubs, nurturing a generation of climate leaders.

Climate Resilience and Early Warning

Working with government institutions, we raise awareness of extreme weather, early warning systems and household preparedness to protect lives, livestock and livelihoods.

Sustainable Living

We promote responsible consumption, food waste reduction, recycling and composting at household and community level.

Stitching a Path to Self-Reliance

Women Empowerment · Muslim Colony, Islamabad

In Muslim Colony, many women had talent and determination but no training, equipment or way to earn. Some were widows raising children alone, some depended on husbands with irregular daily-wage work, and others had skills they had only ever used at home. SOS Foundation launched stitching and embroidery classes for women and girls, and through a follow-up programme supported by our donors and volunteers, provided sewing machines to women in need.

What followed was a quiet transformation. Farha, a mother of three who once relied on others for everything, now stitches suits and school uniforms for her neighbours. Her earnings pay for her children's school supplies and help with the rent.

"Earlier, I waited for help with everything. Now I earn for myself." (Farha)

Nazia, widowed with two young children, now runs a tailoring service from a corner of her home and no longer depends on relatives each month.

"Now my children see that their mother works and earns on her own." (Nazia)

Sakina turned her gift for embroidery into orders for shawls and bridal suits, and she now teaches the skill to girls on her street. Other women have joined together to take bulk orders from local shops, so a single machine supports several families. One programme has grown into a circle of opportunity that keeps widening.

"What I received, I am now passing on to others." (Sakina)

A Daily Meal, Served with Dignity

Health and Nutrition · Multan

Rasheed, a construction labourer, works long, gruelling hours under Multan's scorching sun. His wages come and go and food prices keep rising, so a proper meal was often the first thing he gave up, so that his family back home could eat.

SOS Foundation's daily cooked food distribution brings hot, nutritious meals to Multan's labour community, prepared and served under safe food-handling and hygiene practices. Workers also learn about handwashing and food safety to protect themselves from illness. For Rasheed, a daily meal means the strength to work a full day, and more of his earnings sent home to his children. A simple plate of food, served with respect, tells every worker that their wellbeing matters.

"After a hard day's work, this meal gives me strength. It feels like someone cares about us." (Rasheed, Multan)

Mobility with Dignity: Wheelchairs for PIMS Patients

Health and Nutrition · PIMS, Islamabad · In collaboration with Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS)

Abdul Rehman, a 62-year-old from a modest family in Islamabad, could barely walk after surgery. Every visit to the hospital for check-ups and tests meant his son had to hold him up through long corridors, because the hospital’s old wheelchairs were worn out and often already in use. For families already spending on medicines and travel, buying a wheelchair of their own was out of the question.

SOS Foundation, in collaboration with PIMS, donated 30 wheelchairs to the hospital. They replaced worn-out mobility aids and gave patients who cannot walk a safe, comfortable way to reach wards, labs and clinics. Abdul Rehman no longer has to wait or be supported on his feet. He reaches his appointments in comfort, and his family no longer has to struggle to carry him. A wheelchair may look like a simple piece of equipment, but for the patient who uses it, it restores independence, dignity and easier access to care.

“Now I can go for my treatment without being a burden on my family.” (Abdul Rehman, PIMS)

Today she reads her grandchildren's storybooks, signs her own name and checks her household accounts with confidence. When an adult learns to read, the whole family learns too.

"I used to put my thumbprint on everything. Now I write my own name." (Shamim, Rawalpindi)

"My children are not falling sick like before. Clean water has given us peace of mind." (Nasreen, Mumtazabad)

At ten years old, Ali had never sat in a classroom. In Sohan, on the edge of the federal capital, poverty, distance and the cost of books kept many children like him out of school, and each passing year made catching up harder.

Together with BECS, SOS Foundation helped create a learning space where these children could begin again. Children enrolled in accelerated learning programmes received complete educational kits. For Ali, as for many others, it was the first school bag and books he had ever owned. His teachers soon noticed a boy who arrived early, kept his books carefully wrapped and was eager to answer questions. Every child who returns to the classroom brings Pakistan closer to fulfilling Article 25-A of the Constitution and SDG 4.

"Now I have my own books. One day I want to become a teacher." (Ali, Sohan)

Healthcare at the Doorstep in Bari Imam

Health and Nutrition · Bari Imam, Islamabad · In collaboration with the National Health Services Academy (NHSA)

For Zubaida, a mother of four, her own health always came last, after school fees, rent and food for her children. Persistent fatigue and headaches had troubled her for months, but the cost of a doctor and the distance to the hospital kept her at home.

In collaboration with the National Health Services Academy, SOS Foundation organised a free medical camp that brought qualified doctors and volunteers into the heart of Bari Imam. Residents received free check-ups, screening, consultations and medicines, along with health and hygiene awareness sessions. Zubaida was examined for the first time in years, received medicines free of charge and was guided on follow-up care. She left with treatment, and with the knowledge she needed to look after her family's health.

"For the first time, someone asked about my health. I received care without worrying about the cost." (Zubaida, Bari Imam)
